title: Separation conjecture for polynomial roots and isodynamic points
statement:
Let $P$ be a univariate polynomial of degree $d\geq 3$ with at most double roots, and let $\mathcal I_P$ denote its set of isodynamic points. Consider the zero locus of $P(z)$ in the complex plane.

**Separation conjecture.** No circle or line in $\mathbb C$ separates the zero locus of $P(z)$ from $\mathcal I_P$.

This is presented as an analog of Laguerre's theorem concerning the location of roots of polar derivatives. The claim is supported by numerical experiments for randomly rooted polynomials of degrees at least three, but no proof or resolution is supplied.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.01658

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).
source_name: Christian Hägg, Boris Shapiro and Michael Shapiro, “Introducing isodynamic points for binary forms and their ratios”, arXiv:2207.01658 (2022).
